title: Understanding the Logistic Function
text: To calculate the probability of survival, we use the logistic function, which is defined as \( \sigma(z) $$=$$ \frac{1}{1+e**{-z}} \). Here, \( $$z$$ \) is the linear combination of the parameters and features. Can you identify what \( $$z$$ \) would be for a 20-year-old female passenger?

title: Calculating the Linear Combination
text: The linear combination \( $$z$$ \) is calculated using the formula \( $$z$$ $$=$$ \beta_0 + \beta_1 \times \text{age} + \beta_2 \times \text{sex} \). Given the values \( $$\beta=(-1.2, -0.005, 2.5)$$ \), what would \( $$z$$ \) be for a 20-year-old female?

title: Substituting Values into the Formula
text: Substitute the values into the formula: \( $$z$$ $$=$$ $$-1.2$$ + $$(-0.005)$$ \times $$20$$ + $$2.5$$ \times $$1$$ \). Simplify this expression to find \( $$z$$ \).

title: Calculating the Probability
text: Once you have \( $$z$$ \), use the logistic function \( \sigma(z) $$=$$ \frac{1}{1+e**{-z}} \) to find the probability of survival. What is \( \sigma(z) \)?

title: Understanding Cross-Entropy Loss
text: Cross-entropy loss is calculated using the formula \( -\log(\sigma(z)) \) for a positive class (survived). Why do you think this formula is used?
